name: Performance-Weighted Analyst Estimates
description: This dataset applies an enhanced version of the StarMine SmartEstimate model to a broad universe of stocks and financial metrics, leveraging analyst estimate data from IBES. It calculates a performance score for each analyst based on their historical forecasting accuracy and incorporates the recency of their estimates. By combining these two factors, the model generates "smart estimates" that are more predictive than simple consensus means. The dataset includes modules for analyst innovation, outlier handling, and time-series feature generation, making it a robust tool for identifying which analyst forecasts are likely to be most accurate. This can help investors and researchers anticipate earnings surprises and price movements, as changes in smart estimates often precede market reactions.

name: ESG scores
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Reuters Instrument Codes (RICs) and Bloomberg Identifiers (BBIDs), facilitating cross-platform security identification and data integration. By linking these two widely used financial identifiers, the dataset enables seamless aggregation and comparison of market data from Bloomberg and Refinitiv sources. This mapping is essential for portfolio managers, researchers, and trading systems that require accurate and efficient reconciliation of securities across different data vendors. While not directly predictive of price movements, the dataset is crucial for ensuring data integrity and consistency in multi-source financial analysis, which underpins robust quantitative research and trading strategies.

name: Social Media Relation Dataset
description: This dataset extracts and delivers unique keywords from news titles that are specifically associated with individual publicly listed companies. By parsing news headlines from multiple major financial news sources, it identifies keywords that are rare or distinctive to a small set of companies, rather than generic market terms. The dataset includes metadata such as keyword frequency, company associations, and detected inter-company relationships based on shared news context. This information can be leveraged to identify emerging themes, company-specific events, or novel developments that may not be widely recognized by the market yet. As such, it is a valuable tool for event-driven trading strategies and for predicting price movements triggered by unique news catalysts or shifts in company narrative.

name: Estimations of Key Fundamentals
description: This dataset provides daily, regionally split files containing detailed and consensus analyst estimates for key financial metrics such as revenue, EBITDA, EPS, dividends, and price targets for publicly traded companies worldwide. It includes individual analyst and broker forecasts, consensus calculations (mean, median, high, low, standard deviation), and actuals, along with metadata on fiscal periods, reporting currencies, and company identifiers. The dataset is highly granular, supporting point-in-time analysis and backtesting, and is essential for identifying earnings surprises, revisions, and trends in analyst sentiment. By tracking changes in consensus and individual estimates, users can anticipate price movements driven by earnings releases, analyst upgrades/downgrades, and shifts in market expectations.

name: Earnings forecasts
description: This dataset provides bottom-up aggregated earnings forecasts and related financial metrics at the country, sector, industry, and index levels, covering 56 countries and major international indices with history back to 1985. It includes consensus analyst estimates for key measures such as EPS, revenue, book value, cash flow, dividends, P/E ratios, and long-term growth, all calendarized and available in local and common currencies. The data is structured to support global asset allocation, cross-border valuation, sector and industry analysis, and derivatives research. By tracking changes in consensus, estimate revisions, and aggregated sentiment, the dataset enables investors to identify under- or overvalued markets, monitor macro and sector trends, and anticipate shifts in market sentiment—making it a valuable tool for predicting price movements at both the index and sector level.

name: Real Time Estimates
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Bloomberg IDs (BBIDs) and Reuters Instrument Codes (RICs), facilitating cross-referencing of securities across two major financial data platforms. The mapping is maintained and updated to ensure accurate linkage, supporting workflows that require integration of Bloomberg and Reuters data, such as security master management, trade reconciliation, and multi-vendor analytics. While not intended for general research or direct price prediction, the dataset is essential for ensuring data consistency and completeness in quantitative models and operational processes that rely on both Bloomberg and Reuters identifiers.

name: USA Analyst Estimate Daily Data
description: This dataset provides comprehensive historical performance statistics for individual equity analysts and their institutions, focusing on US equities. It includes detailed metrics such as forecast accuracy (probability of hitting price targets), revision accuracy (improvement of forecasts over time), consistency (standard deviation of forecast errors), and profitability (average returns from following analyst forecasts). The data is available at both the analyst and estimator (institution) level, with relative rankings and normalized scores among peers covering the same stock. These metrics enable quantitative investors to identify top-performing analysts, filter out consistently poor forecasters, and construct weighted consensus forecasts, thereby improving the predictive power of analyst-based signals for price movements.

name: Analyst Estimate Data for Equity
description: This dataset provides intraday updates of consensus financial estimates, actuals, and company guidance for over 16,000 global companies, sourced from more than 800 contributing brokers. It includes multiple daily delta files per region, allowing users to track real-time changes in analyst expectations for key financial metrics such as EPS, sales, dividends, cash flow, and industry-specific items. The dataset also offers daily historical consensus timelines, enabling analysis of estimate revisions, surprises, and trends. By capturing the latest market sentiment and analyst forecasts, this data is highly valuable for predicting price movements, identifying earnings momentum, and responding to market-moving events as they unfold.

name: Integrated Broker Estimates
description: WQ SmartData is an intermediate data platform that provides value-added, idea-embedded data managers and analytics for financial and event datasets. It includes advanced processing such as event classification (e.g., M&A, earnings), group clustering, natural language processing of textual data (e.g., EDGAR filings, news sentiment), and graph/network analytics. By integrating and transforming raw data from sources like FactSet, RavenPack, and EDGAR, it enables researchers to extract features, signals, and event-driven alphas that are difficult to obtain from raw feeds, supporting innovative quantitative strategies and improving the predictive power of models for price movements.

name: Analyst Trade Ideas
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Bloomberg IDs (BBIDs) and Refinitiv Instrument Codes (RICs), facilitating cross-platform identification of securities. It is sourced from both Bloomberg and Refinitiv, ensuring high coverage and accuracy. While not intended for general research or direct price prediction, this mapping is essential for data integration, enabling analysts and portfolio managers to link and synchronize datasets from different vendors. By ensuring consistent instrument identification, it supports robust multi-source analytics, backtesting, and the construction of unified trading universes, which are foundational for any quantitative or fundamental price movement analysis.

name: Alternative Analyst Investment Insight Data
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Reuters Instrument Codes (RIC) and Bloomberg Identifiers (BBID) for financial securities. By consolidating identifier information from both Bloomberg and Refinitiv sources, it enables seamless cross-referencing and integration of data from different platforms. While it does not contain price or signal data itself, this mapping is essential for researchers and portfolio managers who need to align datasets, ensure data consistency, and accurately join or compare information across systems. Reliable identifier mapping is a foundational tool for any workflow that involves multi-source data analysis or model building, indirectly supporting more accurate and robust price movement predictions by ensuring data integrity.

name: Analyst Estimation Data
description: This dataset provides comprehensive fundamental data and analyst-driven rankings for over 1,700 primarily US-listed securities, with some international coverage. It includes detailed historical and estimated metrics such as earnings, sales, dividends, valuation ratios, and proprietary rankings for timeliness, safety, and technical performance. The dataset also features forward-looking projections, growth rates, and risk measures, updated monthly until 2014 and weekly thereafter. By combining quantitative financials with qualitative analyst assessments, this resource is valuable for predicting price movements, identifying outperformers, and constructing factor-based or risk-managed investment strategies.

name: Earning Quality Analyst Estimates
description: This dataset provides comprehensive financial and capital offering data for U.S. and global insurance companies, including property & casualty, life, health, and reinsurance sectors. It covers company profiles, ownership structures, security details (common and preferred equity, senior and subordinated debt, trust preferred, GIC-backed notes), offering terms, and transaction-level details such as pricing, maturity, call/put features, and regulatory capital. The dataset also includes extensive financial statement data, key ratios (ROE, ROA, combined ratio, loss ratio), embedded value, solvency metrics, and segment-level performance. With historical and current data, it enables peer benchmarking, trend analysis, and risk assessment. This rich, timely information is valuable for predicting price movements by tracking capital structure changes, new offerings, financial health, and market sentiment in the insurance sector.

name: Fundamental Analyst Estimates
description: The FactSet Fundamental dataset provides comprehensive annual and interim financial statement data, ratios, and per-share metrics for global companies, with coverage starting from 1980 for developed markets and the 1990s for developing markets. The dataset includes restatements, detailed line items, and standardized fields, enabling robust cross-company and cross-market comparisons. Key fields include balance sheet, income statement, and cash flow items, as well as derived ratios such as return on equity, margins, and growth rates. This dataset is valuable for quantitative and fundamental analysis, backtesting, and predictive modeling, as it allows users to track historical financial performance, identify trends, and build factor models that can help forecast future price movements based on company fundamentals.

name: Broker Estimates
description: This dataset provides concise, real-time summaries of major company news events that are likely to move markets. Each event is tagged by topic (such as M&A, earnings guidance, product launches, regulatory actions, and more) and assigned a significance level, allowing users to filter for the most impactful developments. The data includes detailed headlines, descriptions, event categorization, and metadata such as company identifiers, event timing, and industry classification. By focusing on material news and filtering out less relevant information, this dataset enables quantitative analysts and traders to integrate event-driven signals into their models, backtest the impact of specific news types, and react quickly to market-moving corporate actions, thereby improving the prediction of short-term price movements and volatility.

name: Analyst estimate prediction data
description: This dataset provides point-in-time, globally standardized fundamental financial data for over 47,000 active and 15,000 inactive companies across more than 100 countries. It includes daily snapshots of income statements, balance sheets, and cash flow statements, as well as original and restated values, ensuring accurate historical backtesting without forward-looking or survivorship bias. The data is available on both annual and interim bases, with coverage extending back to 1989 for US companies and 1997 for non-US companies. By offering consistent, unbiased, and comprehensive financials, this dataset enables robust factor research, model development, and performance attribution, making it highly valuable for predicting price movements based on fundamental signals and for constructing and validating systematic investment strategies.

name: Smart Conference call transcript data
description: This dataset provides comprehensive coverage of corporate and macroeconomic events, including earnings releases, conference calls, IPOs, SEC filings, and economic indicators. It includes detailed event metadata, verbatim transcripts, analyst briefs, and supporting materials such as presentations and audio recordings. The data is structured with identifiers like RIC, CUSIP, SEDOL, and ISIN, and is updated frequently with both current and historical records. By tracking the timing, content, and sentiment of key corporate events and macroeconomic announcements, this dataset enables investors and analysts to anticipate market-moving news, assess management tone and guidance, and identify catalysts that may impact stock prices and market volatility.

name: Analyst Estimate Daily Data
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Reuters Instrument Codes (RIC) and Bloomberg Identifiers (BBID), facilitating cross-platform security identification. It is sourced from both Bloomberg and Refinitiv, ensuring broad coverage and accuracy. The mapping enables users to link securities across different data providers and trading systems, which is essential for portfolio management, trade reconciliation, and data integration tasks. While not directly predictive of price movements, the dataset is crucial for ensuring data consistency and enabling the use of multiple datasets in quantitative research and trading strategies.

name: Deep Learning Analyst Chart Signals
description: This dataset leverages deep learning to predict stock returns by mimicking how retail traders interpret analyst-driven financial charts. It transforms time series data related to analyst activity and financial measures into images, which are then processed by pre-trained convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to forecast future price movements. By capturing visual patterns and signals that may be overlooked by traditional quantitative models, this approach aims to extract alpha from the collective sentiment and revisions embedded in analyst data. The dataset is particularly useful for identifying non-linear relationships and subtle cues in analyst-driven market behavior, offering a novel edge for systematic trading strategies.

name: Bias Adjusted Analyst Forecasts
description: This dataset provides refined analyst estimates for stock price targets and fundamental metrics, with systematic analyst biases removed. By leveraging both detailed and consensus-level forecasts, it offers bias-controlled measures for key indicators such as price targets and earnings per share. The dataset includes various statistical summaries (mean, median, standard deviation, high/low values) and tracks the frequency of estimate revisions. By eliminating common sources of analyst optimism or pessimism, these bias-free estimates offer a more accurate and reliable view of market expectations. This can enhance quantitative models and investment strategies by improving the predictive power of analyst forecasts for future price movements, reducing noise, and helping to identify genuine signals of market sentiment and company performance.

name: Board Member Network Analysis
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive analysis of company board member networks, focusing on the connections and influence of directors across multiple firms. It includes metrics such as board strength, number of connected companies and individuals, and various network centrality scores (e.g., authority, hub, page rank, betweenness, eigen centrality). By quantifying the structure and reach of board member relationships, the dataset helps identify companies with strong strategic guidance, access to resources, and potential for superior financial performance. Investors and analysts can leverage these insights to predict price movements by assessing how board connectivity and influence may impact company growth, risk management, and competitive positioning.

name: Deep Learning Chart Returns Predictor
description: This dataset leverages deep learning techniques to analyze visual representations of time series financial data, such as stock price charts, to forecast future multi-horizon returns. By emulating the decision-making process of retail traders who rely on chart patterns, the dataset transforms historical price and volume data into images, which are then processed by pre-trained convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to generate predictive signals. The output includes raw and relative return predictions, quantile rankings, and probability scores for individual stocks. This approach can help identify short-term price movements and potential trading opportunities by capturing complex, non-linear patterns in market behavior that traditional quantitative models may overlook, making it a valuable tool for alpha generation and risk management in equity portfolios.

name: Deep Learning Chart Return Prediction
description: This dataset leverages deep learning techniques to analyze visual representations of financial time series data, such as OHLC charts, to predict future stock returns. By imitating the decision-making process of retail traders who rely on chart patterns, the dataset transforms interval-based price and volume data into images, which are then processed by pre-trained convolutional neural networks (CNNs). The model outputs multi-horizon return predictions, quantile rankings, and probabilities for future price movements. This approach enables the identification of complex, non-linear patterns in market data that may be missed by traditional statistical methods, making it a valuable tool for forecasting short-term and medium-term price changes and enhancing trading strategies.

name: Commercial Real Estate Exposure Model
description: This dataset provides a quantitative measure of individual stocks’ sensitivity to the commercial real estate market, using a robust regression approach that controls for residential real estate and interest rate effects. By calculating a “commercial real estate beta” for each stock, the dataset enables investors to identify companies with high or low exposure to commercial real estate risks. Sector-level summaries and firm-specific scores help users assess portfolio vulnerability to market shifts, especially during periods of stress in real estate or credit markets. This information is valuable for risk management, portfolio construction, and tactical asset allocation, as it allows investors to hedge or adjust positions based on anticipated movements in the commercial real estate sector, potentially improving prediction of price movements for affected stocks.

name: Finance Creator Prediction Performance
description: This dataset aggregates and analyzes stock price predictions made by prominent finance content creators across platforms such as Twitter, YouTube, and select Discord channels. Using AI-driven natural language processing and computer vision, it extracts directional signals (long/short), confidence scores, and performance metrics for each creator and asset. The data includes detailed accuracy statistics, momentum indicators, and portfolio returns segmented by market conditions and time horizons. By tracking the historical success and behavioral biases of these creators, the dataset provides a unique perspective on crowd-sourced trading sentiment and can be leveraged to identify emerging trends, high-confidence signals, and potential price movements in equities.

name: Deep Learning Volume Prediction
description: This dataset leverages deep learning techniques to predict future trading volume for stocks by analyzing time series chart images, mimicking the decision-making process of retail traders. It utilizes pre-trained convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to extract features from visual representations of financial data, such as OHLC charts and barcharts, and combines multiple uncorrelated prediction modules (including news count, price-volume averages, and direct volume data) to generate robust volume forecasts. The dataset covers all stocks and incorporates fallback logic using 20-day average volumes to ensure reliability. By providing forward-looking volume estimates, this resource can help identify periods of heightened market activity, anticipate liquidity changes, and improve the timing and risk management of price movement predictions.

name: Earnings Update Emails Data
description: This dataset compiles analyst communications following company earnings releases, focusing on the sentiment and key financial metrics discussed in these emails. By classifying messages based on keywords such as guidance, EBIT, EBITDA, and EPS, and providing an overall sentiment score for each email, the dataset offers a unique perspective on market reactions and analyst outlooks. The information can be leveraged to gauge immediate market sentiment, anticipate price movements, and identify shifts in analyst expectations, making it a valuable resource for predicting short-term stock performance after earnings announcements.

name: International Findings Data
description: This dataset offers daily snapshots of international corporate events, including earnings announcements, conference calls, dividend declarations, shareholder meetings, and other key financial events. It provides detailed metadata such as event status, timing, fiscal period, and confirmation level, along with links to press releases and filings. By tracking the timing and revisions of earnings dates, dividend actions, and other corporate events, the dataset enables researchers and traders to anticipate market-moving disclosures, identify signals of management intent, and exploit calendar-based trading strategies. Its forward-looking coverage and granular event data are valuable for predicting price movements, volatility spikes, and abnormal returns around scheduled corporate actions.

name: Horizon Earnings and Calendar North America
description: This dataset provides concise, real-time summaries of major company news events that are likely to impact market prices. Each event is tagged by topic, significance level, and includes a headline and detailed description, covering a wide range of corporate actions such as mergers, acquisitions, product launches, regulatory changes, earnings guidance, and more. The data is structured for easy integration into quantitative models, allowing users to filter by region, industry, and event type. By focusing on high-impact developments and filtering out less relevant news, this dataset enables analysts and traders to quickly identify actionable events, perform historical trend analysis, and enhance event-driven trading strategies to better predict price movements.

name: Deep Learning Earnings Chart Predictions
description: This dataset leverages deep learning techniques to analyze financial time series charts, specifically focusing on earnings calendar events. By converting historical price and earnings data into images, it utilizes pre-trained convolutional neural networks to predict future stock returns over multiple horizons. The dataset includes quantile-based rankings, probability assignments, and risk-adjusted metrics, making it valuable for identifying stocks likely to outperform or underperform following earnings announcements. Its predictive signals can help traders and analysts anticipate price movements around earnings releases, enhance alpha generation, and improve portfolio decision-making by incorporating retail trader perspectives and advanced image-based modeling.

name: Earnings Event Risk Model
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive quantitative framework for assessing and forecasting the risk associated with upcoming corporate earnings announcements. It integrates options-implied volatility, historical price movements, and advanced statistical techniques to estimate the uncertainty and potential price impact of earnings events. The model identifies stocks with elevated earnings risk, flags potential short-selling candidates, and offers metrics for integrating earnings uncertainty into portfolio risk management. By quantifying earnings-induced volatility and comparing it to realized volatility, the dataset enables investors to anticipate outsized moves, optimize portfolio construction, and hedge against adverse earnings surprises, thereby improving risk-adjusted performance during earnings season.

name: Multi Aspect Earnings Call Sentiment
description: This dataset provides advanced, multi-aspect sentiment analysis of earnings call transcripts for thousands of public companies across the US and Europe. Using state-of-the-art natural language processing and knowledge distillation from large language models, it evaluates sentiment across key financial dimensions such as asset utilization, profitability, leverage, valuation, and cash flow. The transcripts are segmented into presentation, question, and answer sections, with chunk-wise and summary sentiment scores available for each. Binary indicators and relevance scores help filter for the most impactful segments. By quantifying positive, negative, and neutral sentiment at granular and summary levels, the dataset enables investors and researchers to detect shifts in management tone, analyst sentiment, and market outlook, providing valuable signals for predicting future price movements and earnings surprises.

name: US Equity KPI Forecasts
description: This dataset provides forward-looking forecasts of key financial performance indicators for approximately 1,500 US-listed companies, tailored to each firm's sector and business model. Metrics commonly include revenue, gross earnings, EBITDA, and product or segment-level financials, with additional industry-specific KPIs where relevant. The forecasts are generated using an ensemble model that integrates data from over a thousand sources, including public filings and industry data. Each forecast is accompanied by measures of historical accuracy, consensus comparison, and model confidence, enabling users to assess the reliability and potential edge of the predictions. By offering granular, company-level forecasts ahead of earnings releases, this dataset is valuable for anticipating earnings surprises, sector trends, and price movements, supporting strategies such as event-driven trading, portfolio rotation, and risk management.

name: Deep Learning Event Return Prediction
description: This dataset leverages deep learning techniques to predict future stock returns based on event-driven financial data. By transforming time series data—such as price, volume, and event occurrences—into chart images that mimic the perspective of retail traders, the dataset enables convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to extract predictive features. It incorporates modules for handling earnings, news counts, and macroeconomic indicators, and provides both raw and relative return forecasts across multiple time horizons. The dataset is designed to capture the impact of corporate events, news flow, and market sentiment on asset prices, offering actionable signals for long and short trading strategies. Its multi-horizon, cross-sectional ranking and probability outputs make it a powerful tool for anticipating price movements and generating alpha in quantitative trading models.

name: Equity Expected Move Metrics
description: This dataset provides quantitative estimates of the expected price movement for equities over specified time horizons, derived from options market data and volatility metrics. It includes several approaches to calculating expected moves, such as Gaussian and log-normal models, as well as straddle and strangle-based strategies. The dataset also incorporates daily option volume and liquidity filters to ensure robustness. By capturing the market's consensus on future volatility and directional risk, these metrics can be valuable for forecasting price swings, managing risk, and identifying trading opportunities ahead of major market events or earnings releases.

name: Regulatory Filing Sentiment Analytics
description: This dataset provides detailed sentiment analysis of regulatory filings, including annual, quarterly, and event-driven reports submitted by public companies. It parses filings into standardized sections and applies advanced natural language processing to quantify positive and negative sentiment, track changes over time, and summarize key sections such as risk factors and management discussion. By measuring shifts in sentiment, word counts, and thematic topics, the dataset enables investors and analysts to detect changes in corporate tone, risk disclosure, and outlook, which can be predictive of future price movements. The ability to compare historical baselines and monitor sentiment trends across filings offers valuable insights for forecasting returns, identifying market inefficiencies, and constructing alpha-generating strategies.

name: Forward Beta Risk Prediction Model
description: This dataset provides forward-looking estimates of stock beta for U.S. companies, predicting their sensitivity to market movements over the next three months. The model leverages a combination of fundamental, technical, and historical data to generate more accurate beta forecasts than traditional backward-looking measures. It includes alternative risk metrics, uncertainty bands, and risk surprise probabilities, enabling investors to assess systematic risk and anticipate potential volatility shifts. By identifying stocks with changing risk profiles, the dataset supports portfolio construction, risk management, and alpha generation strategies, making it a valuable tool for predicting price movements and managing exposure to market risk.

name: Management and Executive Data
description: This dataset provides comprehensive biographical and professional information on board members and senior executives from companies worldwide. It includes details such as employment history, education, achievements, compensation, board roles, committee memberships, and network connections across organizations. By analyzing board composition, director expertise, compensation structures, and interlocking directorates, investors and researchers can assess governance quality, leadership stability, and potential strategic shifts. These insights are valuable for predicting price movements, as changes in executive leadership, board structure, or director networks often precede significant corporate actions, impact investor sentiment, and influence firm performance.

name: Press Release Data
description: This dataset contains press release information from public companies, typically published a few days before formal SEC filings such as 10-K and 10-Q reports. It includes preliminary earnings announcements, non-GAAP financial metrics, company guidance, and key operating metrics. By providing early insights into company performance and management expectations, the dataset enables investors and analysts to anticipate price movements ahead of official filings. The data is useful for identifying trends, outliers, and market sentiment, making it valuable for short-term trading strategies and event-driven analysis.

name: Comprehensive Fundamentals Dataset
description: The dataset holds fundamental items included in a company's balance sheet, income statement and cash flow statements. Even footnote items are included for enhancements and complete coverage for some companies.

name: Audit Analytics Directors Data
description: This dataset provides comprehensive tracking of director and officer changes for US public companies, including appointments, resignations, dismissals, and other board or executive movements as disclosed in SEC filings (primarily Form 8-K Item 5.02). It includes detailed information on the individuals involved, their roles (e.g., CEO, CFO, board member), the nature and timing of the changes, and related company and auditor data. By monitoring these governance events, investors and analysts can identify potential signals of corporate strategy shifts, management instability, or governance improvements, all of which may precede significant price movements. The dataset is particularly valuable for event-driven strategies, risk assessment, and understanding the impact of leadership changes on company performance.

name: Direct Fundamental Data
description: The FactSet Fundamental dataset provides comprehensive annual and interim financial statement data, ratios, and per-share metrics for global equities, with coverage starting from 1980 for developed markets and the 1990s for emerging markets. The dataset includes restated data from 2004 onward, ensuring historical accuracy and comparability. Key fields cover balance sheet, income statement, and cash flow items, as well as detailed breakdowns of assets, liabilities, equity, revenues, expenses, and key performance indicators. FactSet’s symbology enables robust cross-referencing with other datasets. This dataset is valuable for quantitative and fundamental analysis, backtesting, and model development, as it allows researchers to track company financial health, valuation, and performance over time, supporting predictive modeling of price movements based on changes in core financial metrics.

name: Report Footnotes
description: This dataset provides granular financial statement footnote data for publicly traded companies, extracted using advanced XBRL technology. It includes detailed disclosures on items such as goodwill, deferred taxes, share-based compensation, and other key financial metrics not typically found in headline financial tables. By enabling users to drill down into historical and cross-company footnote information, the dataset offers unique insights into accounting policies, risk exposures, and non-standard financial events. Such depth of information can help analysts identify hidden risks, spot trends in corporate behavior, and improve the accuracy of fundamental models for predicting price movements.

name: Environmental and Social Governance Data
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between two major financial security identifiers: RIC (Reuters Instrument Code) and Bloomberg ID. By linking these identifiers, the dataset enables seamless integration and reconciliation of securities data across platforms, supporting accurate instrument identification in multi-vendor environments. While not directly containing price or fundamental data, this mapping is essential for analysts and quantitative models that aggregate, compare, or merge datasets from different sources. Reliable cross-referencing improves data quality and enables more robust research, trading, and risk management workflows, indirectly supporting price prediction by ensuring correct instrument alignment.

name: Fundamental Point in Time Data
description: This dataset provides point-in-time, globally standardized fundamental financial data for over 60,000 companies, including both active and inactive firms, with daily granularity. It includes original and restated values for income statements, balance sheets, and cash flow statements, as well as business and geographic segment data, ratios, and company metadata. The point-in-time structure eliminates forward-looking and survivorship biases, enabling accurate historical backtesting and model development. With coverage dating back to 1989 for US companies and 1997 for non-US, this dataset is essential for constructing robust factor models, event studies, and alpha signals based on true historical financials, supporting reliable prediction of price movements and risk assessment.

name: Company Operating Metrics
description: This dataset provides comprehensive, standardized financial statement data and key operating metrics for companies covering 96% of global market capitalization. It includes annual and quarterly financials, per share data, calculated ratios, pricing, and textual information, enabling deep peer comparability across industries and regions. The dataset features over 1,500 data items such as income statement, balance sheet, cash flow, segment data, and supplemental metrics, with point-in-time history, restatements, and amendments. Analysts can use this rich dataset to assess company performance, financial health, and valuation, making it highly valuable for predicting price movements, screening for investment opportunities, and building quantitative models.

name: Global Fundamental Data
description: This dataset provides comprehensive, standardized fundamental financial data for public companies worldwide, covering over 96% of global market capitalization. It includes annual and interim/quarterly financial statements, per share data, calculated ratios, pricing, and descriptive company information. With over 1,500 data items, the dataset enables deep peer comparability and historical analysis across regions and industries. It is highly valuable for quantitative research and price prediction, as it allows for the construction of fundamental factors (such as value, quality, profitability, and growth), backtesting of investment strategies, and robust cross-sectional and time-series analysis of company performance and valuation drivers.

name: Fundamentals Data for US Equities
description: This dataset provides comprehensive financial data for over 9,000 U.S. listed public companies, sourced directly from their annual (10-K) and quarterly (10-Q) SEC filings. It includes a wide array of key financial metrics such as revenue, net income, assets, and operating income, all error-checked and normalized for consistency. The data is updated rapidly after new filings, ensuring timely access to the latest financial information. Analysts and investors can leverage this dataset to perform in-depth financial analysis, build quantitative models, and identify trends or anomalies that may signal future price movements, making it a valuable resource for equity research and predictive analytics.

name: Additional Factor Model
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Bloomberg Identifiers (BBID) and Refinitiv Instrument Codes (RIC) for securities. It serves as a cross-reference tool, enabling users to link and reconcile data across platforms that use different security identifiers. While it does not contain price or fundamental data itself, it is essential for integrating datasets from multiple sources, ensuring consistency in security identification, and facilitating more accurate analysis and modeling. This mapping is particularly useful for researchers and portfolio managers who need to merge or compare datasets, track securities across systems, and support robust data management workflows in multi-vendor environments.

name: Energy Fundamental Data
description: This dataset provides comprehensive asset-level, financial, regulatory, and operational data for thousands of electric utilities, natural gas companies, and coal, nuclear, and renewables plants across North America. It includes detailed information on proposed projects, streaming power price and demand data from all major Independent System Operators, and commodity price points for spot, forwards, and futures markets. The dataset also covers rate cases, regulatory events, company identification, and financial metrics such as return on equity, rate base, and capital structure. By integrating market prices, operational performance, regulatory outcomes, and company fundamentals, this resource enables analysts to assess utility and energy company health, forecast price movements, and evaluate the impact of regulatory changes and market dynamics on asset values and stock performance.

name: Company Fundamental Data for Equity
description: This dataset provides comprehensive, point-in-time global company fundamental data, capturing daily snapshots of financial statements, balance sheets, cash flows, and key ratios as they were known to the market at each historical date. It includes restatements, amendments, and all changes, ensuring accurate backtesting and minimizing look-ahead bias. The dataset covers a wide range of standardized and normalized financial metrics across regions and industries, making it a critical resource for quantitative research, factor modeling, and alpha generation. By reflecting the true information set available to investors at any given time, it enables robust prediction of price movements and supports the development of systematic investment strategies.

name: Factor Ratios and its Rank Model
description: Raw Fundamental Ratios and Rank Data. A global time series of the raw data that is used to compute stock factors and the ranks of the factors. Raw ratios are the underlying factor ratios that are calculated using specific methodologies. To compute ranks, we sort the raw ratios in ascending/descending order based on the factor and then rank them from 1 – 100. 1 being the best and 100 the least preferable. The start date for US and US5000 files is 01/01/2009, the start date for non-US files is 01/01/2013.

name: Quarterly Fundamental Data
description: The dataset provides quarterly fundamental data

name: Comprehensive Fundamentals Data
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Bloomberg IDs (BBID) and Reuters Instrument Codes (RIC), enabling users to cross-reference securities across Bloomberg and Refinitiv platforms. It is essential for data integration, linking, and harmonization in multi-vendor environments, supporting accurate security identification for trading, portfolio management, and research workflows. While not directly predictive of price movements, it facilitates the aggregation and analysis of market and fundamental data from different sources, thereby improving the reliability and completeness of quantitative models and backtesting.

name: Comprehensive Fundamental Data
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Reuters Instrument Codes (RICs) and Bloomberg IDs for global securities. It enables users to cross-reference and link securities across two major financial data platforms, facilitating seamless integration of datasets from different sources. The mapping covers a wide range of asset classes and regions, supporting data normalization and consolidation for research, analytics, and operational workflows. By ensuring accurate identifier matching, this dataset is essential for portfolio management, risk analysis, and multi-source data aggregation, ultimately improving the reliability of price movement predictions and historical backtesting.

name: Fundamental Indicators
description: This dataset provides comprehensive aggregate fundamental indicators for a wide range of U.S. stock market industries and sectors. It includes metrics such as gross margin, operating margin, asset turnover, current ratio, debt-to-equity, capital expenditures to sales, free cash flow to sales, sales to enterprise value, EBITDA to enterprise value, book-to-market value, earnings yield, tax rate, return on equity, return on capital, and various dividend-related ratios. The data is organized by industry, sector, and sub-industry using the Global Industry Classification Standard (GICS), and is available as market capitalization-weighted averages, percentiles, and medians. By tracking these aggregated financial health indicators over time, investors and analysts can identify industry trends, assess sector strength or weakness, and generate signals that may help predict future price movements or inform sector rotation strategies.

name: Stock Reports Plus
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Bloomberg IDs and Reuters Instrument Codes (RICs), facilitating the cross-referencing of securities across different financial data platforms. By enabling seamless integration of data from multiple sources, it helps analysts and quantitative researchers ensure accurate security identification and aggregation of information. While not directly predictive of price movements, this mapping is essential for constructing robust multi-source datasets, which can improve the reliability of signals and models used in price prediction and risk analysis.

name: Oil Price Resilience Scores
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Reuters Instrument Codes (RIC) and Bloomberg Identifiers (BBID), facilitating seamless integration and cross-referencing of securities across two major financial data platforms. By enabling accurate identification and linkage of securities, the dataset supports portfolio managers, analysts, and researchers in consolidating data from multiple sources, improving data quality, and reducing operational risk. While not directly predictive of price movements, it is essential for ensuring data integrity in multi-source quantitative models and for efficient trade execution and compliance reporting.

name: SEC Report Data
description: This dataset provides comprehensive, standardized fundamental financial data for global companies, including annual and quarterly balance sheets, income statements, cash flow statements, and key financial ratios. It covers a wide range of metrics such as revenues, earnings, assets, liabilities, equity, and cash flows, as well as detailed industry classifications (GICS, SIC, NAICS), company identifiers (GVKEY, CUSIP, ISIN, SEDOL, ticker), and corporate actions. The data is point-in-time, capturing both original and restated values, and is structured to support robust historical analysis and backtesting. By offering granular, high-quality financials and corporate event data, this dataset enables researchers and investors to build and test predictive models, assess company health, and identify drivers of price movements across global equity markets.

name: Ownership Model Data
description: This dataset provides comprehensive global coverage of equity ownership by institutions, mutual funds, and insiders/stakeholders, with detailed position-level data for each security and holder. It includes both summary and granular holdings, sourced from regulatory filings such as SEC 13F, UK Share Register, and other international disclosures. The data tracks current and historical positions, market values, portfolio characteristics, and investment styles, enabling analysis of ownership trends, concentration, and changes over time. By revealing shifts in institutional and insider holdings, the dataset helps identify informed trading, herding, and market sentiment, which are critical for predicting price movements, liquidity changes, and potential catalysts in global equities.

name: Short Sale Volume Data
description: This dataset provides detailed information on short sale trading activity for U.S. equities, including metrics such as short volume, short exempt volume, total trade volume, and trade-level details like symbol, date, time, size, and price. The data is sourced from multiple trade reporting facilities and covers regular trading hours, offering a comprehensive view of short selling across major U.S. exchanges and off-exchange venues. By analyzing trends in short sale volume relative to total volume, market participants can gauge bearish sentiment, identify potential short squeezes, and anticipate price movements driven by short covering or increased short interest. This dataset is valuable for traders, analysts, and quantitative researchers seeking to enhance predictive models and risk management strategies.

name: Institutions and Beneficial Stake Ownership
description: This dataset provides comprehensive information on global equity ownership by institutions, mutual funds, and beneficial stakeholders. It includes current and historical holdings data from over 50,000 portfolios and companies across 70 countries, with more than 10 years of history. Key fields cover shares held, percent of shares outstanding, report dates, aggregated statistics, and investor profiles. The dataset enables analysis of institutional buying and selling activity, ownership concentration, and changes in major holders, which are critical for understanding market sentiment, liquidity, and potential price movements. By tracking shifts in institutional positions and identifying new or reduced stakes, investors and researchers can anticipate trends, detect accumulation or distribution phases, and enhance predictive models for stock price behavior.

name: Insider Model Data
description: This is an insider dataset based on the trades and holdings of company’s insiders. It provides ranking of stocks based on insiders trading activity. The idea is to use information advantage that insiders have to predict future performance of the stock. It has low correlation to other standard quantitative factors.

name: Index Reconstitution Data
description: This dataset provides comprehensive information on global index reconstitution events, including the addition and deletion of stocks or companies from various equity indexes, their respective weight percentages, and detailed hedge ratio data. It covers dynamic and static hedge ratios for both indexes and currencies, as well as currency pair exposures and effective dates. The dataset also includes metrics such as momentum and interest rates, along with position weights and returns for index components. By tracking changes in index composition, weights, and hedging strategies, this dataset enables analysts to identify shifts in market sentiment, sector rotation, and currency risk management, which are critical for forecasting price movements and understanding the impact of index rebalancing on asset prices.

name: Multi Factor Model Universal Output
description: This dataset provides the output of proprietary multi-factor risk models in a standardized format compatible with widely used risk models such as Barra and Uber. It enables portfolio managers and researchers to access daily, point-in-time factor exposures, risk estimates, and groupings for US equities, facilitating integration with simulation and portfolio construction tools. The dataset leverages advanced machine learning clustering techniques on company fundamentals and price data to create robust, dynamically updated groupings that capture stock co-movement and risk structure beyond static sector classifications. By offering comprehensive, daily-updated risk model outputs, this dataset supports more accurate risk control, portfolio optimization, and alpha signal neutralization, ultimately helping users better predict and manage price movements and portfolio risk.

name: Fundamentals and Technical Indicators Model
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive suite of 274 quantitative fields covering global equities, including regions such as North America, Europe, and Asia. It encompasses a wide range of factor types, such as value, growth, quality, momentum, volatility, liquidity, technical indicators, analyst estimates, and sentiment metrics. The data includes both historical and forward-looking measures, as well as revisions and surprises, enabling robust multifactor modeling and risk analysis. By integrating fundamental, technical, and sentiment factors, the dataset supports the development and backtesting of predictive models for stock selection, portfolio construction, and risk management, making it highly valuable for forecasting price movements and identifying alpha opportunities across global markets.

name: Corporate Patent Innovation Activity Dataset
description: This dataset provides quantitative measures of company innovation and patent activity, including metrics such as innovation relevance, patent citations, originality, diversity, and maintenance events. It covers a broad universe of publicly traded companies, with historical and daily time series data on patent-related factors. The dataset includes sector-neutralized scores and composite innovation signals, which are used in advanced alpha models to identify stocks with strong technological momentum and relevance. By analyzing the evolution and impact of a firm's technology base, the dataset helps investors predict price movements by highlighting companies likely to outperform due to superior innovation, while also supporting market-neutral and pairs trading strategies.

name: Risk Parity Method Model
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive quantitative model for value investing, utilizing dynamic regime switching, risk mitigation techniques, and multifactor analysis. It includes composite scores based on price-to-earnings, dividend yield, free cash flow yield, operating cash flow yield, and book-to-market ratios, all adjusted for sector, exposure, and correlation biases. The model outputs daily and monthly updated scores for the top 3000 US stocks, supporting both market neutral and long-only strategies. By combining adaptive factor exposures and risk parity methods, the dataset helps identify undervalued securities while minimizing downside risk, making it a valuable tool for predicting price movements and constructing robust investment portfolios.

name: Alternative technical factor models
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Bloomberg IDs (BBID) and Refinitiv Instrument Codes (RIC), enabling seamless integration and cross-referencing of securities across major financial data platforms. By facilitating accurate instrument identification, it supports data normalization and aggregation from multiple sources, which is essential for building robust multi-source trading models, conducting security-level research, and ensuring consistency in price and volume analytics. While not directly predictive, this mapping is a foundational resource for linking datasets that can be used to forecast price movements and enhance quantitative research workflows.

name: ETF Based Equity Factors
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive suite of quantitative signals derived from daily ETF activity across over 1,000 US-listed passive equity ETFs, covering more than $3 trillion in assets. It includes detailed metrics on ETF inflows, outflows, net flows, trading intensity, popularity, and changes in ETF holdings at the individual stock level. By aggregating ETF creation and redemption flows, as well as tracking the percentage of shares held by ETFs, the dataset enables users to identify trends in institutional demand, liquidity shifts, and crowding effects. These factors are highly relevant for building multi-factor and cross-sectional risk models, and can be used to predict short-term price movements, mean-reversion opportunities, and potential volatility in US equities.

name: Stock Selection from Accounting-based Factors
description: This dataset contains a comprehensive suite of Performance Deviation Index (PDI) factors derived from 14 key accounting variables, designed to measure the deviation of a company's latest financial metrics from its historical averages. The dataset includes composite models, quality-focused variants, and sector-neutralized signals, all constructed using advanced techniques such as risk parity weighting, deseasonalization, and clustering. By capturing anomalies and behavioral biases in financial statement data, these factors have demonstrated superior risk-adjusted returns compared to traditional accounting ratios and growth metrics. The dataset is valuable for quantitative investors seeking to enhance stock selection, improve portfolio diversification, and boost predictive power for price movements across global equity markets.

name: Sensitivity to the Inflation Change
description: This dataset provides stock-level sensitivity estimates to expected inflation, using changes in breakeven rates and advanced machine learning techniques such as elastic net regression. It covers a wide range of global equities and includes sector, country, and performance metrics, allowing users to analyze how individual stocks and sectors respond to inflationary pressures. By quantifying inflation beta and related exposures, the dataset is valuable for portfolio managers and analysts seeking to forecast price movements, manage risk, and implement tactical asset allocation strategies in environments with changing inflation expectations.

name: Stock Selection DL model
description: This dataset provides the outputs of a next-generation deep learning model designed for global stock selection with a focus on statistical arbitrage and mean reversion alpha. It includes both raw and processed model scores, updated daily and with monthly historical data, covering a broad universe of equities across multiple regions. The model leverages advanced neural network architectures such as CNNs, RNNs, LSTMs, transformers, and conformers, and is engineered to be interpretable and relatively uncorrelated with common equity style factors. The dataset is particularly valuable for systematic and high-frequency trading strategies, as it offers timely, actionable signals that can be used to enhance portfolio construction, manage risk, and exploit short-term price inefficiencies. By providing robust, data-driven alpha signals, this dataset can help predict price movements and improve trading performance.

name: Fundamental Scores

By enabling seamless integration of data from Bloomberg and Refinitiv, it helps analysts and portfolio managers ensure accurate security identification, streamline data aggregation, and reduce errors in multi-source research workflows. While not directly predictive of price movements, this mapping is essential for robust data management, enabling more reliable analysis and backtesting when combining datasets that use different security identifiers.

name: Return prediction from conference call
description: The Reuters Fundamentals Point In Time dataset provides comprehensive, globally standardized financial statement data for public companies, capturing both originally reported and restated values as they were known at each historical date. It covers over 47,000 active and 15,000 inactive companies across more than 100 countries, with daily updates and history extending back to 1989 for US firms and 1997 for non-US. The dataset is designed to eliminate forward-looking and survivorship biases, enabling accurate backtesting and robust quantitative research. By offering point-in-time snapshots of income statements, balance sheets, and cash flow statements, along with detailed metadata on restatements, reporting currency, and auditor opinions, it allows researchers and investors to model and predict price movements based on true historical financial information, supporting factor research, event studies, and systematic investment strategies.

name: ML/AI-Estimates for Analysts' Factor Model
description: This dataset provides market-implied values for quantitative alpha model signals by applying advanced deep learning techniques to vendor-supplied alpha model data, specifically from the QSG factor library. By leveraging price and volume data, the model estimates what the market "implies" about the value of each alpha factor, rather than relying solely on raw or fundamental inputs. The methodology includes dynamic clustering, time-series feature engineering, and dimension reduction to generate robust, uncorrelated groupings and predictions. The resulting market-implied factor values can be used to identify discrepancies between model signals and market expectations, offering a unique perspective for forecasting price movements, detecting potential mispricings, and enhancing alpha generation in systematic trading strategies.

name: Time-series prediction of alpha models
description: The Starmine dataset provides two key quantitative models: the Earnings Quality (EQ) model and the Analyst Revisions Model (ARM). The EQ model ranks global stocks (percentile 1-100) based on the sustainability and reliability of reported earnings, using a multi-factor approach that incorporates accruals, cash flow, operating efficiency, and exclusions (such as the difference between pro forma and GAAP earnings). The ARM model also ranks stocks (percentile 1-100) by tracking changes in analyst sentiment, including revisions to earnings estimates, revenue forecasts, and recommendations. Both models are sector- and region-neutral, and are designed to predict future analyst revisions and price movements. The dataset includes detailed subcomponent scores, flags for data quality, and is available globally with daily updates. These models are widely used for stock selection, risk management, and alpha generation, as they have demonstrated strong predictive power for future returns and can be used to identify stocks with improving fundamentals or deteriorating earnings quality.

name: Research Analyst Estimate Factors
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive weekly snapshot of analyst estimate activity for S&P 500 stocks, including metrics such as the percentage of price target increases and decreases, buy and sell recommendation ratios, net revisions, earnings surprises, and long-term growth forecasts. It also includes measures of analyst coverage and dispersion in earnings estimates, offering insight into market attention and consensus. By tracking changes in analyst sentiment, forecast revisions, and recommendation trends, the dataset helps identify shifts in market expectations and potential catalysts for price movement. Investors and researchers can use these factors to anticipate earnings-related volatility, detect sentiment-driven momentum, and enhance predictive models for stock returns.

name: Fundamental & Technical Rank Model
description: This dataset provides weekly quantitative rankings for a broad universe of U.S. multi-cap stocks by dynamically blending fundamental and technical metrics. The model assigns each stock a score from 0 to 100, reflecting its relative attractiveness based on factors such as profitability, valuation, analyst estimates, risk, and price momentum. The dynamic weighting of these factors adapts to changing market regimes, aiming to identify profitable, high-quality companies trading at favorable multiples and exhibiting strong price action. The dataset includes buy, sell, and neutral signals, as well as backtested performance metrics like Sharpe ratio and drawdown. Investors and analysts can use these rankings to enhance short-term (one- to two-week horizon) stock selection, construct long/short portfolios, and improve the prediction of near-term price movements.

By offering a unified structure and definitions, wqsuperfunda allows researchers to build robust, comparable financial signals and models across regions and time, improving the reliability of backtests and the predictive power of price movement forecasts based on company fundamentals.

By analyzing patterns in insider buying and selling, the dataset helps identify bullish or bearish sentiment among those with privileged access to company information. This can be a valuable predictive signal for price movements, especially when combined with other quantitative factors, and is useful for constructing long-short portfolios, screening stocks, and enhancing multi-factor investment models.

Each security is ranked within its region, country, sector, and industry, enabling cross-sectional analysis and factor diversification. The dataset includes historical scores, mapping files for identifier cross-referencing, and supports backtesting and portfolio construction. By aggregating diverse predictive signals, it helps investors identify bullish and bearish opportunities, optimize long-short strategies, and improve the robustness of price movement forecasts across global markets.

name: Conviction based hedge funds selections
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive suite of quantitative factors and signals derived from hedge fund ownership data, focusing on stock selection and alpha generation. It includes detailed metrics such as changes in ownership levels, position sizes, conviction-weighted trades, and sector-specific stock selection skills, all adjusted for manager conviction and breadth. The data is further enhanced by weighting ownership changes by measures like Alpha-ROE and sector risk-adjusted alpha, offering insights into the efficiency and persistence of alpha generation among top-performing hedge funds. By tracking shifts in hedge fund positions, concentration, and turnover, the dataset enables users to identify potential price movements driven by institutional activity, crowding, and conviction, making it a valuable tool for predicting future stock performance and constructing alpha-seeking investment strategies.

name: Factors Dislocations Data
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive suite of quantitative risk factors for US equities, focusing on market dislocations and distortions that emerged during the global crisis period. It includes monthly data for the top 3,000 US companies, covering metrics such as hedge fund crowding, financial leverage, credit spread sensitivity, interest rate exposure, default risk, and regional sales exposures. The dataset also features composite scores aggregating multiple risk signals. By tracking the stretching and mean-reversion of these factors, investors and analysts can identify periods of heightened risk, sector-specific vulnerabilities, and potential opportunities for portfolio tilting or hedging. The data is particularly valuable for predicting price movements during times of market stress, as it highlights which stocks or sectors are most exposed to systemic shocks and factor distortions.

It harmonizes thousands of balance sheet, income statement, cash flow, and ratio fields, offering both mapped (cross-vendor comparable) and unique (vendor-specific) items. The data is available at both annual and quarterly frequencies and covers global regions, with detailed field definitions and extensive historical backfill. By enabling direct comparison and aggregation of financial metrics across different sources and geographies, this dataset is invaluable for quantitative research, cross-sectional and time-series analysis, and the development of robust, global equity models. Its breadth and consistency make it a foundational resource for predicting price movements based on fundamental drivers, facilitating factor construction, backtesting, and alpha signal generation with reduced survivorship and look-ahead bias.

name: Credit Risk Factors
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive suite of daily credit risk and solvency metrics for publicly traded U.S. companies, derived from detailed capital structure data. It combines traditional credit risk models (such as Altman Z-Score, Ohlson O-Score, CHS, and Merton’s distance-to-default) with alternative, empirically tested insolvency signals to form a composite risk score. The dataset includes granular ratios on debt, equity, liquidity, debt maturity, interest rates, and stress scenarios, as well as model-implied alpha signals for expected excess returns. By capturing both conventional and alternative risk factors, this dataset offers enhanced predictive power for identifying companies at risk of financial distress or default, especially during periods of market stress. Investors and analysts can use these insights to improve stock selection, manage portfolio risk, and anticipate price movements driven by changes in credit quality.

The dataset provides both raw and sector/region-neutralized versions of factors, as well as point-in-time and forward-looking metrics, making it suitable for robust backtesting and live signal generation. With detailed coverage of analyst revisions, earnings surprises, price momentum, liquidity, and risk metrics, this factor library enables systematic investors to construct, test, and optimize multi-factor stock selection models, perform risk attribution, and enhance alpha generation by identifying drivers of excess returns and forecasting future price movements.

name: Text Mining Data
description: This dataset delivers a quantitative assessment of corporate credit risk by systematically analyzing the language used in news articles, conference call transcripts, corporate filings, and broker research reports. By leveraging advanced natural language processing and proprietary scoring algorithms, it generates default probabilities, implied credit ratings, and percentile risk ranks for publicly traded companies. The model captures early warning signals of financial distress and credit deterioration that may not be immediately evident in traditional financial ratios, making it a powerful tool for predicting adverse price movements, managing credit exposure, and enhancing multi-factor investment strategies. Its ability to anticipate defaults and downgrades ahead of market consensus provides a significant edge for both equity and fixed income investors.

name: Valuation Momentum Data
description: This dataset integrates two advanced quantitative models: an earnings quality model that ranks stocks based on the sustainability and reliability of their reported earnings, and an analyst revisions model that tracks changes in analyst sentiment and estimate revisions. The earnings quality component uses a multi-factor approach, considering accruals, cash flow, operating efficiency, and exclusions to assess the likelihood that a company's earnings will persist. The analyst revisions component evaluates the direction and magnitude of recent analyst estimate changes, which have historically been strong predictors of future price movements. By combining these perspectives, the dataset provides percentile rankings (1-100) for stocks globally, enabling investors to identify companies with both robust, sustainable earnings and positive analyst sentiment. This dual approach is highly effective for predicting price movements, as it captures both fundamental strength and market expectations, making it valuable for quantitative managers, stock screeners, and alpha-seeking strategies.

name: Insider Data for the US
description: This dataset provides comprehensive information on equity transactions conducted by individuals and entities classified as insiders within US companies. It includes detailed records of purchases, sales, and holdings of both derivative and non-derivative securities, as reported to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) via Forms 3, 4, 5, and 144. The data covers thousands of companies and hundreds of thousands of insiders, with historical records dating back to 1986. Key fields include transaction type, date, price, number of shares, insider role, and resulting ownership positions. The dataset also features split-adjusted values, cleansing indicators, and average post-transaction returns. By analyzing insider trading patterns, market participants can gain valuable insights into the sentiment and confidence of company executives and major shareholders, which can serve as leading indicators for potential price movements and inform investment strategies.

name: Systematic Risk Metrics

These metrics are particularly valuable for constructing risk-aware portfolios, evaluating hedging strategies, and forecasting price movements based on changes in risk profiles. It includes over 350 stock selection signals spanning value, momentum, quality, growth, risk, liquidity, sentiment, and industry-specific factors, with coverage across developed, emerging, and frontier markets. The dataset provides factor definitions, cross-sectional rankings, and performance analytics, enabling users to identify key drivers of returns and construct robust, diversified investment models. By systematically evaluating fundamental, technical, and specialty signals, the dataset helps investors uncover persistent sources of excess return and improve portfolio performance through data-driven stock selection and risk management.

name: US News Data
description: This dataset integrates real-time news events and market data to capture the immediate and subsequent price reactions of stocks to a wide range of news and corporate announcements. It includes detailed fields such as news headlines, timestamps, price and volume changes across different trading sessions, analyst actions, earnings surprises, and sector-specific news tags. By quantifying the impact of news on price movements at granular intervals (from seconds to hours), the dataset enables users to identify patterns of underreaction, overreaction, and momentum following news releases. This information is highly valuable for developing event-driven trading strategies, backtesting news-based signals, and enhancing alpha generation by systematically exploiting the relationship between news flow and market behavior.

name: PR Edition Data

The data includes detailed event taxonomy, entity mapping, and various sentiment indicators, enabling users to track market-moving news, measure the impact and novelty of events, and assess the relevance of information to specific securities. By quantifying news sentiment and event characteristics, the dataset helps investors and analysts anticipate price movements, identify alpha opportunities, and enhance risk management through timely, data-driven insights.

name: Ravenpack News Data

The data covers a wide range of entities such as companies, products, people, and macroeconomic factors, and is enriched with metadata like event timing, fact level, and source trustworthiness. By quantifying the tone and impact of news stories, this dataset enables investors and researchers to systematically monitor market sentiment, identify significant events, and generate predictive signals for price movements, making it a valuable tool for quantitative trading, risk management, and alpha generation.

name: Future News Data

Each record is tagged with metadata including ticker, industry, announce date and time, news source, and the range of future dates referenced. By systematically extracting and structuring these forward-looking events, the dataset enables investors and analysts to anticipate key corporate actions and market-moving events before they occur. This forward event calendar can be used to forecast volatility, identify trading opportunities around catalysts, and enhance price movement prediction models by aligning news-driven event timing with market data.

The data includes detailed headlines, descriptions, event categorization, and metadata such as timing, company identifiers, and industry classification. By offering structured, noise-filtered news with intelligent tagging, this dataset enables quantitative models and event-driven strategies to quickly identify and react to market-moving information, making it a valuable resource for predicting short-term price movements and volatility.

name: Headline Sentiment Analysis using DNN
description: This dataset leverages advanced machine learning techniques to transfer sentiment signals from one news analytics dataset to another, specifically mapping sentiment derived from one set of financial news headlines onto a different set of press release headlines. By using neural network models to learn how sentiment is constructed in the source dataset and applying this understanding to the target dataset, it generates a new, alternative sentiment score for each press release. This approach enables the creation of a unique sentiment signal that may capture market-relevant nuances missed by traditional sentiment models. Such a dataset can be valuable for predicting price movements, as it provides a differentiated view of market sentiment that can be used to enhance alpha generation, inform trading strategies, and improve risk assessment by identifying shifts in investor mood not visible through standard sentiment analytics.
